# Number of Countable Models of ZFC

## Setting Up the Problem

A **countable model** of ZFC is a structure $(M, \in^M)$ where $M$ is a countable set satisfying all axioms of ZFC. I'll assume ZFC is consistent (the standard working assumption).

## Upper Bound: At Most $2^{\aleph_0}$

The language of set theory contains a single binary relation symbol ($\in$), so it is **countable**. Fixing the domain to be $\omega$ (up to isomorphism, every countable set is $\omega$), a structure is determined entirely by the interpretation of $\in$ as a subset of $\omega \times \omega \cong \omega$.

The number of subsets of $\omega$ is $2^{\aleph_0}$, so:
$$\text{# countable models} \leq 2^{\aleph_0}$$

## Lower Bound: At Least $2^{\aleph_0}$ (up to isomorphism)

I need to show there are at least $2^{\aleph_0}$ **non-isomorphic** countable models.

**Step 1: ZFC is incomplete.** By Gödel's first incompleteness theorem, ZFC (being consistent, recursively axiomatizable, and extending sufficient arithmetic) cannot be complete.

**Step 2: ZFC has $2^{\aleph_0}$ complete consistent extensions.** The set of all complete theories extending ZFC forms a closed subset of the Cantor space $2^{\omega}$ (the space of all complete theories in the countable language). Since ZFC is incomplete, this closed set has **no isolated points**: for any finite set of sentences decided, incompleteness guarantees another sentence splits the remaining space. A non-empty perfect subset of $2^{\omega}$ has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$.

**Step 3: Each complete extension has a countable model.** By the **Completeness Theorem**, each consistent extension of ZFC has a model. By the **Downward Löwenheim–Skolem Theorem** (applicable since the language is countable), each has a **countable** model.

**Step 4: Models of different complete theories are non-isomorphic.** Isomorphic structures satisfy exactly the same sentences, so models satisfying different complete theories cannot be isomorphic.

Therefore:
$$\text{# non-isomorphic countable models} \geq 2^{\aleph_0}$$

## Conclusion

Combining the upper and lower bounds:

$$\text{Number of countable models of ZFC} = 2^{\aleph_0}$$

$$\boxed{2^{\aleph_0}}$$
